identity.spiritualSignificanceShort: Mahakaleshwar is counted among the twelve Jyotirlingas, and its lingam is held to be swayambhu — self-manifested rather than ritually installed. Uniquely among the twelve, the idol is dakshinamurti, facing south, a feature the tantric tradition treats as distinctive to this shrine. Ujjain was long a reference centre for Indian timekeeping, and Mahakala is revered as the presiding deity of the city and as lord of time.

governance.establishedEra: Ancient shrine with a long history of destruction and rebuilding; the standing temple is substantially an eighteenth-century Maratha-period reconstruction
governance.managingAuthority: Administered by the municipal body of Ujjain under the oversight of the district collectorate, following the post-1947 transfer from the Mahakaleshwar Dev Sthan Trust

narrative.documentedHistory:
Ujjain's Shaiva shrine has a long recorded history of destruction and rebuilding. The temple was dismantled in 1234-35 during the raid of Iltutmish, and tradition holds that the Jyotirlinga was thrown into the nearby Kotiteerth Kunda. Further attacks are recorded under Jalaluddin and Alauddin Khalji.

The standing temple is substantially a product of the eighteenth-century Maratha period; Madhya Pradesh Tourism dates the construction to the fourth and fifth decades of the eighteenth century, and Wikipedia attributes the reconstruction to Ramachandra Sukthankar. After Indian independence in 1947 the management of the temple passed from the Mahakaleshwar Dev Sthan Trust to Ujjain's municipal body, and it is now overseen through the district collectorate.

In the twenty-first century the surroundings were substantially rebuilt as the Shri Mahakal Lok corridor, a development of more than 900 metres carrying 108 pillars, over 200 statues and murals drawn from the Shiva Purana.
narrative.architectureStyle: A blend of Bhumija, Maratha and Chalukya idioms, with the shrine arranged over five levels including an underground chamber

visitingInfo.officialContactNote: Darshan and aarti timings recorded here come from the Madhya Pradesh Tourism Board page and are not a live schedule. Bhasma Aarti in particular is capacity-limited and subject to advance registration; confirm current timings, registration rules and any festival-day changes with the temple administration before travelling. The MP Tourism helpline listed on the state tourism page is 1800-233-7777 (Monday to Friday, 10:00-18:00).
visitingInfo.notes: Airport distance is given as 53 km by the Ujjain district and divisional portals, 55 km by MP Tourism and 58 km by Wikipedia; 53 km is recorded here as the government figure.

openingHours.notes: MP Tourism states the temple operates continuously through the day with no afternoon closure. Festival days, Mahashivaratri and Shravan Mondays alter access substantially.

poojas.description: The temple's signature pre-dawn ritual, in which ash is offered to the lingam. Madhya Pradesh Tourism states the ash used is prepared from cow dung. Attendance is capacity-limited and requires advance registration; the specific registration procedure is not recorded here because it could not be read from the temple's own site.

festivals.significance: The principal Shaiva observance of the year at this Jyotirlinga.
festivals.processionOrRituals: A large fair is held near the temple and worship continues through the night.
festivals.crowdNote: Among the heaviest crowd days of the year at the temple.

festivals.gregorianRuleOrDate: Shravana Shukla Panchami; falls in July or August
festivals.significance: The one day in the year on which the Nagchandreshwar idol on the third storey of the temple is opened to visitors.

festivals.gregorianRuleOrDate: Held during the months of Shravana and Bhadrapada
festivals.significance: A processional outing of the deity through the city, a distinctive Ujjain observance.
festivals.processionOrRituals: The procession includes a ceremonial police salute and worship of the deity at the Shipra ghat.

shrines.locationDescription: The main sanctum, housing the swayambhu lingam, which faces south in the dakshinamurti form. Nandi is placed to the south, and images of Ganesh, Parvati and Kartikeya stand at the cardinal points of the sanctuary.
In the sanctum directly above the Mahakaleshwar shrine.
On the third storey of the temple; opened to visitors only on Nag Panchami.
A corridor of more than 900 metres approaching the temple, carrying 108 pillars and over 200 statues and murals drawn from the Shiva Purana.
